questions.q: Why is Russia vulnerable to invasion from the west?
a: A flat plain runs from Europe to Moscow
Its rivers freeze and block its defenses
Its borders follow high mountain ranges
Its population is spread too thinly
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes the North European Plain as flat ground that an army could cross straight to Moscow.

questions.q: What strategy has Russia used to protect itself?
a: Keeping control of Poland and the Baltic states
Building walls along its European border
Moving its capital further to the east
Forming alliances only with southern states
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Russia holds this territory to absorb the vulnerable land and defend more easily.

questions.q: Why is the United States so hard for an army to invade?
a: Oceans border it and its neighbors are friendly and huge
Its mountains split the country into narrow passes
Its climate makes most of the year impossible to cross
Its allies guard every approach by sea
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the oceans and the size of friendly neighbors make invasion logistics nearly impossible.

questions.q: What extra factor does the summary add to America's natural defenses?
a: Widespread ownership of guns by civilians
A very large standing army
A network of coastal fortresses
Strict control of its borders
questions.why: Lesson 2 says easy access to guns means invaders would face armed civilians in nearly every city.

questions.q: Why does the summary say Southern Europe has struggled economically?
a: It has far less arable land than the north
It was slower to industrialize by choice
Its workers lack education and skills
Its governments taxed trade too heavily
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the south has less fertile soil, so it developed fewer major cities of commerce.
